question: Does active learning work well when fine-tuning large language models?

sections.title: Does active learning work well when fine-tuning large language models?
sections.text: Active learning demonstrates strong effectiveness in fine-tuning large language models, achieving comparable results with significantly less training data and showing substantial performance improvements.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Active learning and fine-tuning are two key concepts in the context of large language models (LLMs):

-   Active learning: A machine learning paradigm where the algorithm selectively chooses the most informative data points for labeling. This approach aims to maximize model performance while minimizing the amount of labeled data required.

-   Fine-tuning: The process of adapting a pre-trained LLM to a specific task or domain by further training it on a smaller, task-specific dataset.

The integration of active learning with LLM fine-tuning is significant due to the substantial computational resources and large amounts of labeled data typically required for fine-tuning LLMs. By selectively choosing the most informative examples for fine-tuning, active learning has the potential to:

1.  Reduce the amount of labeled data needed
2.  Decrease annotation costs
3.  Lower computational requirements

This is particularly crucial in domains where labeled data is scarce or expensive to obtain.

The current state-of-the-art approaches in LLM fine-tuning often involve:

-   Fine-tuning on large, diverse datasets
-   Using few-shot learning techniques

However, these methods can be data-intensive and may not always yield optimal results for specific tasks or domains. Active learning offers a promising alternative by focusing on the most valuable data points, potentially leading to more efficient and effective fine-tuning processes.

sections.title: Summary
sections.text:
Active learning can enhance the fine-tuning of large language models by reducing labeled data requirements while maintaining competitive performance. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880c" paperTitle="Osband et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880a" paperTitle="Schröder et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> In several studies, uncertainty‐based sampling led to label efficiency gains of 56.2% on average or allowed performance to match full fine-tuning with roughly 50% less data. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998806" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998809" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880c" paperTitle="Osband et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper> One study reported that using only 0.4% to 15% of training data yielded up to a 14.4-point improvement in the area under the learning curve, and another noted accuracy improvements between 10% and 24% alongside rare-class F₁ score gains of 17%--40%. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880a" paperTitle="Schröder et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880e" paperTitle="Beck et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

Researchers show that adapting active learning strategies---through methods such as novel uncertainty estimation, dynamic uncertainty measurement, and combinations with parameter-efficient approaches like LoRA---can effectively target informative examples. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> A few findings caution that traditional uncertainty sampling may not always perform well, prompting alternative strategies based on prediction score differences. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880f" paperTitle="Bansal and Sharma, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880f" paperTitle="Bansal and Sharma, 2023" isShortName></Paper> Overall, the papers demonstrate that active learning methods yield efficient data usage and sustained task performance when fine-tuning large language models. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880c" paperTitle="Osband et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880a" paperTitle="Schröder et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998806" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998809" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper>

Analysis of quantitative effects:

### Label Efficiency Gain

-   We found label efficiency gain information in the abstracts of 6 out of 10 studies:
    -   3 studies reported a 56.2% improvement on average <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998806" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998809" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper>
    -   2 studies reported a 50% reduction in queries or data <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880d" paperTitle="Ji et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880c" paperTitle="Osband et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper>
    -   1 study reported using 0.4% to 15% of training data <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880a" paperTitle="Schröder et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper>
-   We didn\'t find label efficiency gain information in the abstracts of 4 out of 10 studies <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880f" paperTitle="Bansal and Sharma, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880e" paperTitle="Beck et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880b" paperTitle="Vysogorets and Gopal, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

### Performance Metrics

Performance metrics varied across studies:

-   3 studies used label efficiency as a metric <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998806" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998809" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper>
-   2 studies reported performance similar to or the same as baseline methods <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880d" paperTitle="Ji et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880c" paperTitle="Osband et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper>
-   2 studies reported improvements in accuracy or F-1 score <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880f" paperTitle="Bansal and Sharma, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880e" paperTitle="Beck et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>
-   1 study each reported significant gains, matching state-of-the-art performance, learning curve improvement, and outperforming baseline models <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880f" paperTitle="Bansal and Sharma, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880d" paperTitle="Ji et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880a" paperTitle="Schröder et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

### Statistical Significance

We didn\'t find mention of statistical significance in the abstracts of any of the 10 studies. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880f" paperTitle="Bansal and Sharma, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880e" paperTitle="Beck et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880d" paperTitle="Ji et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880c" paperTitle="Osband et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880a" paperTitle="Schröder et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880b" paperTitle="Vysogorets and Gopal, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998806" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998809" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

sections.text:
### Uncertainty Estimation Approaches

A recurring theme across the studies is the use of uncertainty-based methods for active learning in LLM fine-tuning. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880c" paperTitle="Osband et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998806" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998809" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> However, the specific approaches to uncertainty estimation vary:

1.  Traditional uncertainty-based sampling <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998806" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998809" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   According to their abstracts, several studies, including Liu et al. (2022), Yu et al. (2021), and Yu et al. (2022), employ uncertainty-based sampling as a core component of their active learning strategies. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998806" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998809" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper>
    -   These approaches typically select high-uncertainty samples for annotation and low-uncertainty samples for self-training. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998806" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998809" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper>

2.  Novel uncertainty estimation <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880c" paperTitle="Osband et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   The abstract of Osband et al. (2022) introduces the concept of epistemic neural networks (ENNs) using an \"epinet\" to estimate model uncertainty. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880c" paperTitle="Osband et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper>
    -   This approach allows the model to \"know what it doesn\'t know,\" potentially leading to more effective data prioritization. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880c" paperTitle="Osband et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper>

3.  Challenges with traditional methods <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880f" paperTitle="Bansal and Sharma, 2023" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   Interestingly, the abstract of Bansal and Sharma (2023) reports that popular uncertainty-based sampling strategies do not work well in their context, leading them to propose a novel sampling strategy based on prediction score differences between the base model and the fine-tuned model. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880f" paperTitle="Bansal and Sharma, 2023" isShortName></Paper>

4.  Dynamic uncertainty measurement <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   According to their abstract, Zhang et al. (2024) address the challenge of the \"uncertainty gap\" by introducing a dynamic uncertainty measurement that combines uncertainties from both the base model and the full model during active learning iterations. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

These varying approaches to uncertainty estimation highlight the ongoing research in optimizing active learning strategies for LLM fine-tuning, with a trend towards more sophisticated and LLM-specific methods. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880f" paperTitle="Bansal and Sharma, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880c" paperTitle="Osband et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998806" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998809" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

### Data Efficiency and Resource Requirements

A significant theme across the studies is the focus on improving data efficiency and reducing computational resources required for LLM fine-tuning:

1.  Label efficiency <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880c" paperTitle="Osband et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880a" paperTitle="Schröder et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998806" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998809" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   Multiple studies report substantial improvements in label efficiency. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880c" paperTitle="Osband et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880a" paperTitle="Schröder et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998806" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998809" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper>
    -   According to their abstracts, Liu et al. (2022), Yu et al. (2021), and Yu et al. (2022) all report a 56.2% improvement in label efficiency on average. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998806" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998809" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper>
    -   The abstract of Osband et al. (2022) reports achieving the same performance with 2x less data. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880c" paperTitle="Osband et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper>

2.  Computational efficiency <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880b" paperTitle="Vysogorets and Gopal, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880b" paperTitle="Vysogorets and Gopal, 2024" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   The abstract of Vysogorets and Gopal (2024) focuses on drastically reducing computational costs while maintaining similar performance to full fine-tuning. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880b" paperTitle="Vysogorets and Gopal, 2024" isShortName></Paper>
    -   Their approach is described as \"orders of magnitude less computationally expensive.\" <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880b" paperTitle="Vysogorets and Gopal, 2024" isShortName></Paper>

3.  Query efficiency <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880d" paperTitle="Ji et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   According to their abstract, Ji et al. (2024) introduce query-efficient RLHF methods, with their ADPO algorithm making about half the queries for human preference compared to traditional methods while maintaining performance. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880d" paperTitle="Ji et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

4.  Cold-start scenarios <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880e" paperTitle="Beck et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   The abstract of Beck et al. (2024) reports addressing the challenge of class imbalance and cold-start scenarios, demonstrating improvements in overall accuracy and rare-class F1 scores even with limited initial data. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880e" paperTitle="Beck et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

These findings collectively suggest that active learning can significantly enhance the efficiency of LLM fine-tuning, both in terms of labeled data requirements and computational resources. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880e" paperTitle="Beck et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880d" paperTitle="Ji et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880c" paperTitle="Osband et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880a" paperTitle="Schröder et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880b" paperTitle="Vysogorets and Gopal, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880b" paperTitle="Vysogorets and Gopal, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998806" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998809" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper> This is particularly valuable given the large scale of modern language models and the often high costs associated with data annotation and model training. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b199880e" paperTitle="Beck et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998809" paperTitle="Yu et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper>

### Integration with PEFT Methods

An emerging theme is the integration of active learning with Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) methods:

1.  LoRA integration <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   According to their abstract, Zhang et al. (2024) propose the STAR approach, which combines LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) with dynamic active learning. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>
    -   This integration aims to address the challenges of applying active learning in the context of PEFT methods. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

2.  Challenges in integration <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   The abstract of Zhang et al. (2024) highlights that simply combining PEFT methods with active learning can yield inferior results, pointing to specific challenges such as the uncertainty gap and poor model calibration. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

3.  Novel solutions <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   To address these challenges, the abstract reports that Zhang et al. (2024) introduce techniques such as dynamic uncertainty measurement and regularization methods during LoRA training. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

This theme reflects the ongoing efforts to make LLM fine-tuning more efficient, not only in terms of data usage but also in terms of parameter updates. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> The integration of active learning with PEFT methods represents a promising direction for future research, potentially leading to even more efficient fine-tuning processes for large language models. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

### Model Calibration and Reliability

Several studies address the importance of model calibration and reliability in the context of active learning for LLM fine-tuning:

1.  Overconfidence mitigation <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   According to their abstract, Zhang et al. (2024) incorporate regularization methods during LoRA training to prevent the model from becoming overconfident. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>
    -   This addresses the challenge of poor model calibration, which can affect the effectiveness of uncertainty-based active learning strategies. <Paper corpusId="4f821c440a0d4b0f7eeb4c83b1998808" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

question: During pre-training, why is the transformer embedding layer initialized randomly, rather than with pre-trained embeddings from existing models?

sections.title: During pre-training, why is the transformer embedding layer initialized randomly, rather than with pre-trained embeddings from existing models?
sections.text: Transformer embedding layers are randomly initialized to ensure efficient training and broad applicability while avoiding the potential mismatches and resource overhead of pre-trained embeddings.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Transformer models are a type of neural network architecture that has revolutionized natural language processing tasks. These models use self-attention mechanisms to process and understand sequential data, such as text. Within transformer models, the embedding layer plays a crucial role in converting input tokens (words or subwords) into continuous vector representations that the model can process.

The initialization of the embedding layer is a critical step in the pre-training process of transformer models. This research question focuses on the choice between two main approaches:

1.  Random initialization: Assigning random values to embedding vectors from a specified distribution.
2.  Pre-trained initialization: Using embedding vectors from existing models that have already been trained on large datasets.

The significance of this research question lies in its potential impact on:

-   Model performance on downstream tasks
-   Training efficiency and convergence speed
-   Transfer of knowledge between models
-   Adaptability to specific domains or languages

Current approaches in the field vary, with researchers exploring:

-   Random initialization for its simplicity and potential flexibility
-   Pre-trained embeddings for leveraging existing knowledge
-   Hybrid approaches combining elements of both methods
-   Task-specific adaptation techniques

Understanding the trade-offs between these initialization methods is crucial for developing more efficient and effective transformer models, especially as they continue to grow in size and complexity.

sections.title: Summary
sections.text: Transformer models often begin pre-training with randomly initialized embedding layers because studies show that such initialization offers a robust, efficient foundation despite mixed performance gains from pre-trained embeddings. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009c" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Singh and Giovanardi, "How much does pre-trained information help?"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="El Boukkouri et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper> For example, Chen et al. (2021) achieved 45--47% computational cost savings using a knowledge-transfer variant, and Samragh et al. (2023) recorded 4× faster training via weight subcloning. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Chen et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Samragh et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Samragh et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> In contrast, while Shen et al. (2021) reported BLEU improvements---from 29.45 to 34.14 on IWSLT14 and from 17.29 to 25.24 on WMT14---when using pre-trained weights, Kim et al. (2024) observed that in some cases random initialization outperformed certain pre-trained strategies. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009d" paperTitle="Shen et al., 2021" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009c" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> Other studies note that pre-trained embeddings can be particularly effective in low-data regimes (Singh and Giovanardi) or specific domains (El Boukkouri et al.), yet they also introduce extra resource and domain-adaptation challenges. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Singh and Giovanardi, "How much does pre-trained information help?"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="El Boukkouri et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper> These findings support the common practice of using random initialization to avoid potential mismatches and overhead associated with pre-trained embeddings while maintaining broad applicability across diverse tasks. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009c" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="El Boukkouri et al., 2022" isShortName></Paper>

sections.text:
### Impact of Dataset Characteristics

-   Data Scarcity <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Singh and Giovanardi, "How much does pre-trained information help?"" isShortName></Paper>: Singh and Giovanardi found pre-trained initialization more beneficial with limited training data <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Singh and Giovanardi, "How much does pre-trained information help?"" isShortName></Paper>
-   Domain Specificity: El Boukkouri et al. (2022) observed weak influence of initial corpus when further pre-trained on domain-specific data
-   Model Size <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Turc et al., 2019" isShortName></Paper>: Turc et al. (2019) noted enhanced generalization potential even for compact networks with pre-trained initialization <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Turc et al., 2019" isShortName></Paper>

sections.title: For different modulation types like MPSK, QPSK, and MQAM, I'm measuring the error rate but want to understand and measure the Error Vector Magnitude (EVM) more accurately. I'm using a general equation for all modulation types. Is this the right approach, and what should I expect from the EVM vs. Eb/No curve?
sections.text: While using a universal EVM equation is valid, accurate measurements require modulation-specific correction factors, with EVM versus Eb/No relationships varying by modulation type.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Error Vector Magnitude (EVM) is a crucial metric in digital communications that quantifies the difference between ideal and actual signal constellation points. It provides a comprehensive measure of signal quality by capturing various impairments such as noise, distortion, and modulation errors. In modern communication systems, various modulation schemes are employed to efficiently transmit data. These include Multiple Phase Shift Keying (MPSK), Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (QPSK), and Multiple Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (MQAM).

The accurate measurement and understanding of EVM across different modulation types are essential for optimizing system performance, assessing signal quality, and estimating bit error rates. Traditionally, EVM measurement techniques have been tailored to specific modulation schemes. However, there is growing interest in developing a general approach that can be applied across various modulation types.

This research question addresses the validity of using a universal equation for EVM measurement and seeks to understand the expected relationship between EVM and the ratio of energy per bit to noise power spectral density (Eb/No) for different modulation schemes. The findings from this review will contribute to the ongoing efforts to standardize EVM measurement across diverse communication systems and modulation types.

sections.title: Summary
sections.text:
Fatadin (2016) and Mahmoud and Arslan (2009) show that a general equation for EVM measurement can work across modulation types if proper, modulation‐specific correction factors are applied. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper> For example, studies on QPSK and 64‑QAM report error vector magnitudes that agree within 1% to 3% when EVM remains below 10%, and Manurkar et al. (2020) achieved a nominal value of 1.4% for 64‑QAM using predistortion techniques. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Mckinley et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper> In optical channels with additive Gaussian noise, Freude et al. (2012) and Nebendahl et al. (2012) obtain reliable bit error rate predictions in the 10⁻⁶ to 10⁻² range via EVM measures. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Freude et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>

Analytical models also relate EVM to SNR, implying that EVM versus Eb/No curves will differ with modulation scheme and system impairments. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper> In sum, using a universal EVM equation is a viable approach provided that modulation‐specific nuances are incorporated; the resulting EVM versus Eb/No curve is expected to vary according to modulation type and channel conditions. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper>

-   Modulation types <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Hudlička et al., 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2006" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Mckinley et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   We found mention of modulation types for 8 out of the 10 studies in our review. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Hudlička et al., 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2006" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Mckinley et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>

        -   64-QAM (4 studies) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2006" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Mckinley et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper>
        -   QPSK (3 studies) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Hudlička et al., 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Mckinley et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper>
        -   16-QAM (2 studies) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Hudlička et al., 2016" isShortName></Paper>
        -   QAM (unspecified) (2 studies) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>

-   EVM measurement methods <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Freude et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Hudlička et al., 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2006" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Mckinley et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   Methods varied widely across studies:
        -   Experimental methods (4 studies) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Freude et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Mckinley et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>
        -   Simulation, analytical, and theoretical methods (3 studies each) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Freude et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2006" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>
        -   Other methods (practical, real-time sampling, predistortion, Monte Carlo) (1 study each) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Hudlička et al., 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper>
    -   Many studies used multiple measurement methods. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Freude et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2006" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>

-   System parameters <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Freude et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Hudlička et al., 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2006" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Mckinley et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>:

        -   One reported agreement within 1% to 3% when EVM \< 10% <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Mckinley et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper>

-   Measurement accuracy <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Freude et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2006" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   We found mention of measurement accuracy information for 8 out of the 10 studies:
        -   3 studies reported reliable BER estimation <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Freude et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>
        -   2 studies reported good agreement with measurements <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2006" isShortName></Paper>
        -   1 study each reported reliable SNR estimation, specific percentiles, and \< 1% error <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper>

-   Eb/No Range <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Freude et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Hudlička et al., 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2006" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Mckinley et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   We didn\'t find mention of Eb/No Range information in the abstracts or available full texts of the studies. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Freude et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Hudlička et al., 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2006" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Mckinley et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>

The lack of consistent reporting on Eb/No ranges across studies highlights a potential area for future research to better understand the relationship between EVM and Eb/No for different modulation schemes. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Freude et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Hudlička et al., 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2006" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Mckinley et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>

sections.title: Thematic Analysis
sections.text:
# Thematic Analysis

## EVM Measurement Approaches

### General vs. Specific Equations {#general-vs-specific-equations}

The studies reviewed present a mix of general and specific approaches to EVM measurement and analysis:

-   Some researchers focus on developing models for specific modulation schemes or system configurations. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2006" isShortName></Paper>
-   Others aim for more generalized methods. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>

Key findings:

-   Fatadin (2016) proposed a method to estimate BER from EVM for M-ary QAM formats in optical coherent systems, suggesting that a general approach can be applied with appropriate correction factors. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper>
-   Mahmoud and Arslan (2009) derived equations for EVM to SNR conversion applicable to both QAM and PAM signals, indicating potential for a more universal approach. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper>
-   Hegazi and Do (2024) focused on modeling EVM for a specific modulation scheme (32-APSK) based on particular system characteristics (AM/AM and AM/PM). <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper>

These findings suggest that while general approaches can be useful, there may be benefits to tailoring EVM measurement and analysis to specific modulation types or system configurations. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2006" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>

### Accuracy Considerations

The accuracy of EVM measurement and its relationship to other performance metrics is a recurring theme across the studies:

-   Several researchers report high accuracy in their EVM-based estimations and predictions. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Freude et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2006" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>
-   Nassery et al. (2013) claimed their analytical model for EVM calculation in OFDM transmitters achieved less than 1% error for a large range of EVM values. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper>
-   Manurkar et al. (2020) demonstrated precise EVM measurements with a nominal value of 1.4% and well-defined uncertainty bounds. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper>

These findings suggest that both general and specific approaches to EVM measurement can achieve high accuracy when properly implemented and calibrated to the system under study. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Freude et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Kim et al., 2006" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>

sections.title: Performance Relationships
sections.text:
### EVM vs. Eb/No Patterns {#evm-vs-ebno-patterns}

While the studies reviewed do not provide explicit EVM vs. Eb/No curves, they offer insights into the relationships between EVM and other performance metrics:

-   Freude et al. (2012) and Nebendahl et al. (2012) both found that EVM is a reliable quality measure for optical channels with additive Gaussian noise, particularly for estimating BER in the range of 10\^-6 to 10\^-2. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Freude et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>
-   These findings indicate that in systems dominated by additive Gaussian noise, there may be a relationship between EVM and other performance metrics, which could potentially extend to Eb/No. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Freude et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>
-   Mahmoud and Arslan (2009) derived equations relating EVM to SNR for nondata-aided receivers, which could potentially be extended to relate EVM to Eb/No. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper>

Their work indicates that the relationship between these metrics may be modulation-dependent and affected by channel conditions. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Freude et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Nebendahl et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper>

### Modulation Impact

The impact of modulation scheme on EVM performance and its relationship to other metrics is evident in several studies:

-   Mckinley et al. (2009) found that EVM levels for QPSK and 64QAM agree closely (within 1% to 3%) when EVM is less than 10%. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Mckinley et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper>
-   This suggests that for some modulation schemes, a general approach to EVM measurement and analysis may be appropriate under certain conditions. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Mckinley et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper>
-   However, the focus on specific modulation schemes in studies like Hegazi and Do (2024) for 32-APSK and the varying approaches for different QAM orders in Fatadin (2016) indicate that modulation type can significantly impact EVM behavior and its relationship to other performance metrics. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Hegazi and Do, 2024" isShortName></Paper>

sections.title: Implementation Insights
sections.text:
### Practical Considerations

The studies reviewed offer several practical insights for implementing EVM measurement and analysis:

1.  Impairment Modeling <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   Nassery et al. (2013) emphasized the importance of considering multiple impairments simultaneously when modeling EVM in OFDM transmitters. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper>
    -   This suggests that a comprehensive approach to impairment modeling may be necessary for accurate EVM measurement across different modulation types. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper>

2.  Predistortion Techniques <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   Manurkar et al. (2020) demonstrated the effectiveness of predistortion techniques in achieving low EVM, even at high frequencies (92.4 GHz). <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper>
    -   This highlights the potential for signal processing techniques to improve EVM performance across various modulation schemes. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Manurkar et al., 2020" isShortName></Paper>

3.  Real-time Measurement <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Hudlička et al., 2016" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   Hudlička et al. (2016) used real-time sampling systems for EVM measurement, indicating the importance of considering measurement system capabilities when implementing EVM analysis. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Hudlička et al., 2016" isShortName></Paper>

### Recommendations

Based on the findings from the reviewed studies, the following recommendations can be made regarding the use of a general equation for EVM measurement across different modulation types:

1.  Consider Modulation-Specific Factors <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper>:

    -   While a general approach can be useful, it may be necessary to incorporate modulation-specific correction factors or adjustments, as suggested by Fatadin (2016). <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper>

2. 3.  Incorporate Impairment Models <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Nassery et al., 2013" isShortName></Paper>:

4.  Consider Complementary Metrics <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Fatadin, 2016" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Freude et al., 2012" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Mahmoud and Arslan, 2009" isShortName></Paper>:

question: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) receivers can provide a reference clock signal known as Pulse-per-Second (PPS or 1-PPS). Is the PPS physically generated through a digitally-controlled oscillator (or line driver) whose offset is periodically re-initialized by the estimated clock bias (retrieved by means of PVT algorithms)?

sections.title: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) receivers can provide a reference clock signal known as Pulse-per-Second (PPS or 1-PPS). Is the PPS physically generated through a digitally-controlled oscillator (or line driver) whose offset is periodically re-initialized by the estimated clock bias (retrieved by means of PVT algorithms)?
sections.text: GNSS timing systems typically generate 1-PPS signals through digitally-controlled oscillators that are adjusted based on clock bias estimates derived from satellite timing references.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) provide precise timing and positioning capabilities for a wide range of applications. At the core of GNSS timing functionality is the Pulse-per-Second (PPS or 1-PPS) signal, a critical component for synchronizing local clocks with the highly accurate atomic clocks aboard GNSS satellites. The PPS signal is typically a square wave with a rising edge precisely aligned to the start of each Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) second, serving as a reference for timing applications in fields such as telecommunications, scientific research, and financial systems.

The generation and maintenance of an accurate PPS signal involve complex interactions between hardware and software components:

-   Local oscillators: Devices that generate a continuous, periodic signal
-   Disciplining algorithms: Sophisticated software that adjusts local oscillators to maintain synchronization with GNSS time
-   GPS-disciplined oscillators (GPSDOs): Systems that combine the long-term stability of GPS signals with the short-term stability of high-quality local oscillators

Common types of oscillators used in PPS generation include:

-   Temperature Compensated Crystal Oscillators (TCXOs)
-   Oven Controlled Crystal Oscillators (OCXOs)

The disciplining process often involves algorithms that estimate and correct for clock bias, potentially utilizing Position, Velocity, and Time (PVT) solutions derived from GNSS measurements. Understanding the exact mechanisms of how these systems generate and maintain accurate PPS signals is crucial for advancing timing technology and improving the reliability of time-dependent systems.

sections.title: Summary
sections.text: GNSS timing systems generate 1‐PPS signals by disciplining a local oscillator using satellite‐derived timing references. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper> Several studies describe implementations in which digital signal processing techniques---such as ramp‐predictive finite impulse response filters, phase-locked loops, recursive algorithms, and direct digital synthesis---adjust oscillator frequency based on estimated clock bias. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper> For example, Arceo-Miquel et al. (2009) and Shmaliy et al. (2009) use FIR filters to reduce sawtooth errors, while Liu et al. (2003) and Wang (2011) employ PLL-based and recursive methods to correct phase errors. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper> Reported performance spans sub-nanosecond accuracies (including ≤0.4 ns and values around 20--100 ns under different conditions) and stability metrics as low as 2×10\^-12 at 1 second. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020b" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper> Although not every study explicitly details a digitally-controlled oscillator that is periodically reinitialized using clock bias estimates, the evidence indicates that many GNSS 1‐PPS systems incorporate digital control mechanisms to steer oscillator performance in synchrony with GNSS timing signals. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper>

-   We identified 11 different implementation methods mentioned across the 10 studies. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020b" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper>
-   The most common methods were:
    -   FIR filter (2 studies) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper>
    -   PLL (2 studies) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper>
-   Other methods (e.g., GPS disciplined oscillator, GNSS simulator, statistical processing) were each mentioned in 1 study. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020b" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper>

Hardware Components:

-   We found information on hardware components for 9 out of 10 studies. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020b" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper>
-   The most common components were:
    -   GPS-locked crystal clock (2 studies) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper>
    -   GPS disciplined oscillator (2 studies) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020b" isShortName></Paper>
    -   OCXO (2 studies) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper>
-   Other components (TCXO, quartz oscillator, crystal oscillator) were each mentioned in 1 study. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper>
-   We didn\'t find hardware component information for 1 study. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper>

Synchronization Approaches:

-   We found information on synchronization approaches for 9 out of 10 studies. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper>
-   The most common approach was:
    -   GPS 1PPS (3 studies) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper>
-   Other approaches (e.g., GPS disciplining, GPS/GLONASS PPS, clock bias estimates) were each mentioned in 1 study. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper>
-   We didn\'t find synchronization approach information for 1 study. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020b" isShortName></Paper>

The studies we reviewed demonstrate considerable diversity in implementation methods, hardware components, and synchronization approaches. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020b" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper> GPS-based technologies were commonly mentioned for both hardware and synchronization. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper>

Timing Accuracy:

-   We didn\'t find specific timing accuracy information for 6 out of 10 studies. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper>
-   Of the 4 studies reporting timing accuracy:
    -   1 reported sub-nanosecond precision <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020b" isShortName></Paper>
    -   1 reported ≤0.4 ns <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper>

-   We found information on compensation methods for 9 out of 10 studies. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper>
-   The most commonly mentioned methods were:
    -   FIR filters (2 studies) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper>
    -   Low-pass filters (2 studies) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper>
-   Other methods included alternating operation modes, statistical processing, PLL-based techniques, real-time corrections, and various synchronization and error elimination approaches. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper>

The studies we reviewed showed a diverse range of approaches to timing accuracy, stability metrics, error sources, and compensation methods, reflecting the complexity and variety of timing systems and their applications. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020b" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper>

sections.title: Thematic Analysis
sections.text:
# Thematic Analysis

## PPS Generation Mechanisms

The studies we reviewed reveal a common trend in PPS generation mechanisms: the use of disciplined oscillators, particularly those synchronized with GPS signals. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> While the specific implementation details vary, most approaches involve a local oscillator whose frequency is controlled or disciplined by reference signals from GPS or other GNSS. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper>

The process of generating the PPS signal typically involves:

1.  Receiving timing signals from GPS/GNSS satellites <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper>
2.  Estimating the local clock bias relative to GPS time <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper>
3.  Adjusting the local oscillator frequency to maintain synchronization <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper>
4.  Generating a precise pulse aligned with the start of each UTC second <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper>

While our research question specifically asks about digitally-controlled oscillators, the studies do not uniformly address this aspect. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020b" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper> However, the prevalent use of digital signal processing techniques and programmable logic implementations suggests a trend towards digital control mechanisms. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper>
