sections.title: Clock Discipline Techniques
sections.text:
A key theme emerging from the studies is the variety of clock discipline techniques employed to maintain accurate synchronization. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper> These techniques range from relatively simple phase-locked loops (PLLs) to more sophisticated algorithms involving predictive filtering and statistical signal processing. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper>

Several studies highlight the use of finite impulse response (FIR) filters for clock steering:

-   Arceo-Miquel et al. (2009) and Shmaliy et al. (2009) both propose ramp-predictive FIR filters to optimize clock synchronization and eliminate sawtooth errors inherent in 1PPS signals. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper>

Other notable techniques include:

-   Statistical signal processing to estimate clock bias in the presence of non-Gaussian jitter (Fuhrmann et al., 2014) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper>
-   Precise Point Positioning (PPP) for high-stability clock disciplining (Rønningen and Danielson, 2019) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper>
-   Recursive algorithms for jitter suppression when GPS signals are temporarily unavailable (Wang, 2011) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper>

These diverse approaches reflect the ongoing challenge of maintaining precise synchronization across various environmental conditions and application requirements. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper>

sections.title: Performance and Reliability
sections.text:
The performance and reliability of PPS generation systems are critical themes across the studies. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020b" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper> While the specific metrics and methodologies vary, there is a consistent focus on improving timing accuracy and stability. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020b" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Rønningen and Danielson, 2019" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper>

Short-term stability:

-   Often characterized by metrics such as Allan deviation or time interval error <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper>
-   Schulz and Rüffer (2022) report short-term frequency stability of 2x10\^-12 at 1 second and 5x10\^-12 at 10 seconds for their OCXO-based system <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper>

Long-term stability:

-   Typically addressed through continuous disciplining with GPS signals, as seen in multiple studies <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Fuhrmann et al., 2014" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Shmaliy et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper>

Reliability during GPS signal loss:

-   Xianghui (2009) demonstrates that their system can maintain 100 ns accuracy even after one hour of GPS signal loss <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Xianghui, 2009" isShortName></Paper>
-   Other studies implement holdover modes or alternative disciplining techniques to maintain performance during signal outages <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Wang, 2011" isShortName></Paper>

The trade-off between cost and performance is also evident:

-   Some studies focus on low-cost GPS disciplined oscillators (Bauer et al., 2020a) <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper>
-   Others employ more sophisticated and potentially expensive setups involving OCXOs and advanced signal processing techniques <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Liu et al., 2003" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Schulz and Rüffer, 2022" isShortName></Paper>

The thematic analysis reveals a field characterized by ongoing innovation in both hardware and software aspects of PPS generation. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Arceo-Miquel et al., 2009" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Bauer et al., 2020a" isShortName></Paper> <Paper question: Have large langauge models been applied to the schema matching problem in databases and are they effective?

sections.title: Have large langauge models been applied to the schema matching problem in databases and are they effective?
sections.text: Large language models have proven effective for database schema matching, achieving comparable or better results than traditional supervised systems through multiple implementation approaches.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Schema matching is the process of identifying corresponding elements between different database structures. It\'s like finding common ground between two different ways of organizing information. For example, one database might call a field \"Customer Name,\" while another uses \"Client ID\" - schema matching helps connect these related concepts.

Large Language Models (LLMs) are advanced artificial intelligence systems trained on vast amounts of text data. They can understand and generate human-like language, making them potentially useful for tasks that involve interpreting and connecting different ways of expressing similar ideas.

The application of LLMs to schema matching represents a significant shift in addressing long-standing challenges in database integration. Traditional methods often struggle with semantic differences and complex schemas, requiring extensive domain knowledge or manual intervention. LLMs offer potential advantages in this area:

-   Natural language understanding: LLMs can interpret schema elements described in natural language, potentially capturing semantic nuances.
-   Contextual awareness: LLMs can consider broader context when making matching decisions.
-   Generalization: LLMs trained on diverse datasets may adapt across different domains and schema structures.
-   Automation potential: LLMs may reduce the need for human experts in the matching process.

sections.title: Summary
sections.text:
Large language models have been applied to schema matching in databases using diverse approaches. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Chugh and Zambre, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Xu et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> Zero-shot and few-shot prompting techniques achieve performance comparable to supervised systems, as shown by Hertling and Paulheim (2023). <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> For example, Chugh and Zambre (2024) report a 15% gain in precision and a 7% increase in recall, while Gu et al. (2023) note a 10--20% improvement in execution accuracy over other language model methods. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Chugh and Zambre, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper>

Retrieval-enhanced methods combine natural language understanding with external knowledge: Sheetrit et al. (2024) describe significant matching improvements without retraining, and Ma et al. (2025) report precision gains of 35.89% (MIMIC) and 69.20% (Synthea) alongside F1 score increases of 30.50% and 21.97%, respectively. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> Hybrid architectures that merge rule-based and generative models yield F1 score improvements of 11.84% and offer a 5.08% boost in AUC, as documented by Zhang et al. (2024). <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> Overall, the studies indicate that large language models can effectively address semantic ambiguities and automate schema matching, with measured improvements across key performance metrics. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Matentzoglu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Xu et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

-   We didn\'t find any metrics for precision in 8 studies, recall in 9 studies, and F1 score in 7 studies. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Matentzoglu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Parciak et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Xu et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

sections.title: Thematic Analysis
sections.text:
# Thematic Analysis

## LLM Integration Approaches

### Zero-shot and Few-shot Methods

Several studies explore the potential of zero-shot and few-shot learning approaches in Large Language Model-based schema matching:

-   Hertling and Paulheim (2023) report that zero-shot and few-shot prompting with Large Language Models can achieve results comparable to supervised systems, even with minimal examples. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper>
-   Gu et al. (2023) propose a zero-shot Natural Language to SQL framework that combines pre-trained language models for schema alignment and Large Language Models for complex reasoning. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> They report that their approach outperforms both Pre-trained Language Model-based and Large Language Model-based methods in execution accuracy. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper>

These studies suggest the potential of zero-shot and few-shot methods in reducing the need for extensive training data and manual intervention in schema matching tasks, based on their reported results. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> However, the effectiveness of these approaches may vary depending on the complexity of the schemas and the specific domain. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper>

### Retrieval-Enhanced Techniques

Retrieval-enhanced techniques emerge as a prominent theme in Large Language Model-based schema matching approaches:

-   Sheetrit et al. (2024) introduce ReMatch, a retrieval-enhanced Large Language Model method that they report significantly improves matching capabilities without requiring predefined mapping or model training. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> This approach addresses the challenge of accessing source schema data, which is often a limitation in traditional methods. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>
-   Ma et al. (2025) propose KG-RAG4SM, a Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation model that combines Large Language Models with knowledge graph retrieval. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> They report substantial improvements in precision and F1 score over state-of-the-art methods, particularly in resolving semantic ambiguities and mitigating hallucination problems associated with Large Language Models. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper>

These retrieval-enhanced approaches showcase the potential of combining Large Language Models with external knowledge sources or structured representations to improve the accuracy and robustness of schema matching tasks. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

### Hybrid Architectures

Several studies explore hybrid architectures that combine Large Language Models with other techniques:

-   Liu et al. (2024) introduce Magneto, a two-phase pipeline that combines small language models and large language models to balance computational efficiency and matching accuracy. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper>
-   Zhang et al. (2024) propose SMUTF, a hybrid approach that integrates rule-based feature engineering, pre-trained language models, and generative Large Language Models. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> They report significant improvements in F1 score and Area Under the Curve of Receiver Operating Characteristic over state-of-the-art models. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

These hybrid architectures represent a promising direction in Large Language Model-based schema matching, as they allow for the integration of domain-specific knowledge and established techniques with the semantic understanding capabilities of Large Language Models. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

sections.title: Implementation Considerations
sections.text:
### Knowledge Integration

A recurring theme in the reviewed studies is the importance of integrating domain knowledge and contextual information into Large Language Model-based schema matching approaches:

-   Ma et al. (2025) demonstrate the effectiveness of incorporating knowledge graphs to enhance Large Language Model performance in schema matching tasks. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> They report that their KG-RAG4SM model shows significant improvements in resolving semantic ambiguities and conflicts, which are common challenges in schema matching. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper>
-   Xu et al. (2024) introduce a Knowledge-Compliant Matching Framework (KcMF) that uses pseudo-code-based task decomposition and mechanisms like Dataset as Knowledge and Example as Knowledge to build domain knowledge sets. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Xu et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Xu et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> They report that this approach addresses the challenge of lacking unstructured domain knowledge and helps reduce confusion in Large Language Model reasoning. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Xu et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

These studies highlight the importance of developing methods to effectively integrate domain-specific knowledge and contextual information into Large Language Model-based schema matching systems to improve their accuracy and robustness. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Xu et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Xu et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

### Scalability and Performance

Scalability and performance optimization emerge as crucial considerations in the implementation of Large Language Model-based schema matching systems:

-   Liu et al. (2024) address this challenge with their Magneto framework, which combines small and large language models. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper> They report that this approach reduces runtime without compromising matching accuracy, demonstrating the potential for developing cost-effective and efficient Large Language Model-based solutions for schema matching. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper>
-   Zhang et al. (2024) emphasize the importance of scalability in their SMUTF approach, which they report is designed for large-scale tabular data schema matching and works seamlessly with existing pre-trained embeddings, classification methods, and generative models. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

These studies underscore the need to balance the capabilities of Large Language Models with practical considerations such as computational efficiency and scalability, especially when dealing with large-scale schema matching tasks in real-world applications. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

sections.title: Comparative Effectiveness
sections.text:
### Advantages over Traditional Methods

The reviewed studies consistently report significant advantages of Large Language Model-based approaches over traditional schema matching methods. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Chugh and Zambre, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Matentzoglu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Parciak et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Xu et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> Key advantages include:

-   Improved accuracy <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Chugh and Zambre, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Matentzoglu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Xu et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>: Multiple studies report substantial improvements in precision, recall, and F1 scores compared to state-of-the-art methods. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Chugh and Zambre, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Matentzoglu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Xu et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>
-   Reduced need for training data <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Chugh and Zambre, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>: Several approaches, particularly those using zero-shot and few-shot learning, report effective performance with minimal or no domain-specific training data. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Chugh and Zambre, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>
-   Enhanced semantic understanding <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper>: Large Language Model-based methods are reported to show superior ability in resolving semantic ambiguities and capturing complex relationships between schema elements. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper>
-   Flexibility and adaptability <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>: Many Large Language Model-based approaches report good generalizability across different domains and schema types. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>
-   Automation potential <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Matentzoglu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Parciak et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>: Large Language Model-based methods show promise in reducing the need for manual intervention and speeding up the schema matching process, according to several studies. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Matentzoglu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Parciak et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

These reported advantages highlight the potential of Large Language Model-based approaches to address long-standing challenges in schema matching and improve the efficiency and effectiveness of data integration tasks. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Chugh and Zambre, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Matentzoglu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Parciak et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Xu et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

### Current Limitations

Despite the promising results, several limitations and challenges of Large Language Model-based schema matching approaches are evident from the reviewed studies:

-   Computational resources <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Chugh and Zambre, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Matentzoglu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>: Some approaches, particularly those using large language models, may require significant computational resources, which could limit their practical applicability in certain scenarios. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Chugh and Zambre, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Matentzoglu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>
-   Sensitivity to context <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Parciak et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>: Some studies note that the performance of Large Language Model-based methods can be sensitive to the amount and quality of context information provided. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Parciak et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>

Addressing these limitations will be crucial for the continued development and widespread adoption of Large Language Model-based schema matching techniques in real-world applications. <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a7" paperTitle="Chugh and Zambre, 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a2" paperTitle="Gu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a4" paperTitle="Hertling and Paulheim, 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a3" paperTitle="Liu et al., "Magneto: Combining Small and Large Language Models"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a0" paperTitle="Ma et al., "Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation"" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a1" paperTitle="Matentzoglu et al., 2023" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009e" paperTitle="Parciak et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae009f" paperTitle="Sheetrit et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a5" paperTitle="Xu et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper> <Paper corpusId="cff599f34605423bc9a7464a03ae00a6" paperTitle="Zhang et al., 2024" isShortName></Paper>
